# lila.math

Unreal-flavoured vector math.

```
from lila.math import Vector, Rotator, Transform
v = Vector(1, 2, 3)
t = Transform(Rotator(yaw=90), Vector(0, 0, 100))
t.transform_position(v)
```

Lila space is right-handed, cm, Y-up by default (set_up_axis("z") for Z-up scenes):

```
up axis   FORWARD   RIGHT   UP
y         +Z        -X      +Y
z         +X        -Y      +Z
```

Rotator angles mean what they mean in Unreal on those axes: yaw turns forward toward right, pitch turns forward toward up, roll turns up toward right. Quat, axis-angle and rotate_angle_axis are plain right-handed math. Transform and Matrix compose like Unreal: a * b applies a, then b.

to_unreal / from_unreal convert vectors, quats, rotators, transforms, matrices and boxes to and from Unreal space (left-handed Z-up, X forward, Y right): FORWARD -> +X, RIGHT -> +Y, UP -> +Z.

## Rotator

```python
Rotator(pitch: float = 0.0, yaw: float = 0.0, roll: float = 0.0) -> None

Rotator(quat: lila.math.Quat) -> None

```

Pitch, yaw, roll in degrees with Unreal's meaning on Lila's FORWARD/RIGHT/UP axes: yaw turns forward toward right, pitch turns forward toward up, roll turns up toward right.
